newsitem.title: USA: TV content ratings bill introduced in Senate.
newsitem.headline: TV content ratings bill introduced in Senate.

text.p: A bill to make television broadcasters develop and use content-based ratings for their programs was introduced Thursday by Sen. Dan Coats.

Coats, an Indiana Republican, said the current system started in January is ineffective because it gives only general ratings such as G, for programs that all ages can watch, and TV14, for programs that are inappropriate for children younger than 14.

"A television ratings sytem that does not give parents information on sex, violence and language is no ratings system at all," Coats said in a statement. "The current ratings system is highly ineffective. It doesn't help parents determine the content of the television shows their kids may want to watch."
His bill would bar the Federal Communications Commission from renewing broadcast licenses unless the applicants have a content-based ratings system for their programs.
The bill would prohibit the FCC from establishing a specific ratings system. Instead, the agency would review each rating content system to see that it meets the requirement set by the bill.
